title: Agents that live in MIRROR's interview call
decision: How should MIRROR build the live brain of the interview room, as a complete system?

options.label: The Room: persistent Interviewer + silent Observer + code Director, event-driven
Per-turn orchestrator + one fast call, bank fallback (earlier verdict)
Full panel of speaking agents from day one
End-to-end realtime voice model as the live brain

graham.reason: Will testers feel listened to, and does it change what they do next

musk.reason: Real constraint, simplest architecture, what to delete

blakely.reason: Does it feel alive and loved enough that people tell friends, without scaring them

buffett.reason: Downside: latency, quota, vendor, privacy and the no-scores trust promise

brief: The founder wants agents that live in the interview call, not a question list. The earlier council backed a per-turn orchestrator and rejected serial agents on every turn. This session tests persistent event-driven agents (A), the earlier verdict (B), a full panel (C) and an end-to-end realtime voice model (D), and asks for the complete build.
assumptions: A handful of testers, no revenue (assumed)
Free-tier hosted model with rate limits (assumed)
Two weeks to something that works at beta, more time for the full build (assumed)
